title: feat(types): ObjectGridSchema's zod mirror declares ten members its TypeScript twin declares (objectui#6152 round 6)
body:
Part of #6152 (round 6). The card stays open: `ObjectGridSchema.resizableColumns` stops here with an open question (below), the three spec-derived pairs route to objectui#2231, and the two chatbot `displayMode` entries stay by decision (objectui#7654 ruling B).

Clause-②: yes
Why yes (mixed): the strict face widens on an `object-view`'s `table` slot, where nine keys it refused as unknown are now declared. The tolerant face narrows there and on the flat mirror: a wrongly typed value it kept unexamined is now refused at the key. No TypeScript declaration changes shape.

## Round 6 in one paragraph

`ObjectGridSchema`'s `UnmirroredDeclared` entry held eleven keys. Each was measured first: authored writers in both repositories, readers by a type-checker census and a runtime probe through the real `SchemaRenderer` and registry, and the member of the spec's `ComponentPropsMap['object-grid']` row. Ten are MIRRORED on the flat zod `ObjectGridSchema`: `aggregations`, `bulkActionDefs`, `conditionalFormatting`, `grouping`, `navigation`, `operations`, `reorderableColumns`, `rowColor`, `rowHeight` and `singleClickEdit`. The eleventh, `resizableColumns`, is NOT retired: the seat's answer A predates objectui#11276, which moved the authored node into the spec's `properties` bag, and executing it now would leave that bag accepting a key nothing reads (open question below). `UnmirroredDeclared` goes from 5 entries / 16 keys to 5 / 6 (spec-derived 3 / 14 to 3 / 4; local 2 / 2 unchanged).

## Measured first (base `50c73fed0`)

**H1 held.** A TypeScript-parser count of `interface UnmirroredDeclared` at the base reads 5 entries / 16 keys, with 11 on `objectql.zod.ts#ObjectGridSchema`, the eleven the claim names. `KnownDrift` 49 / 86, `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` 5 / 30 and `RuntimeOnlyNamedAllowList` 4 / 23 read the same at the base, at `main` `401611b2` and at this head.

**H2: the authoring side is the spec's for all eleven.** A one-off probe through the built faces (`AnyComponentSchema`, `StrictAnyComponentSchema`, the spec row, the flat mirror):
- written flat on an `object-grid` node, every one of the eleven is refused by name on both faces, toward `properties.KEY` (`flatPropRefusals`);
- in the bag, the spec row judges it: `reorderableColumns`, `resizableColumns` and `singleClickEdit` as booleans, `bulkActionDefs` as an array of unknown entries, and the other seven as `unknown` (a `properties.grouping: 42` parses on both faces);
- in an `object-view`'s `table` slot, which is built from the flat mirror: nine keys were kept unexamined by the tolerant face and refused as unknown keys by the strict face, while `navigation` and `resizableColumns` are refused by name (withheld).

So the remaining question per key is the hoisted node's parity (the TypeScript `ObjectGridSchema`, which `ObjectGrid` reads) and the `table` slot that inherits the mirror.

**H3: every key is read.** Type-checker census over `packages/*/src` and `apps/*/src` (5697 files; controls `objectName` 58 reads, `columns` 13, `resizable` 2): every key has a src read in `ObjectGrid`, and `ObjectView` reads `table.operations` and relays six more through `tableRelay`. The first census run read 0 for the `objectName` control: its file list had dropped every file directly under a `src/` root. That run was discarded and the enumeration fixed. Runtime probe (one-off, deleted): an authored node `{ type: 'object-grid', properties: { … } }` through the real registry, varying one key, with a fetch double recording every request. Every key changed the drawn markup or the adapter calls:

| key | runtime reading (base) |
| --- | --- |
| `aggregations` | the group header query gains a `sum` of `amount`, and the header draws it |
| `bulkActionDefs` | after a row is selected, the bulk bar draws the def's button |
| `conditionalFormatting` | the matching row gains its `background-color` |
| `grouping` | the grid asks `queryGroupHeaders` and draws grouped sections |
| `navigation` | clicking a row opens the drawer overlay |
| `operations` | `export: false` removes the export button that `exportOptions` draws |
| `reorderableColumns` | header cells become `draggable="true"` |
| `resizableColumns` | `false` removes the column resize handle (no `resizable` written) |
| `rowColor` | the row's background class changes |
| `rowHeight` | the row-height toolbar appears |
| `singleClickEdit` | absent, one click opens the cell editor; `false`, it does not |

Controls: the same document rendered twice is byte-identical; `columns` changed (the lit control) differs. A first run was stopped by the repository's network-escape guard (a permission read reached a real socket) and its readings were discarded; the recorded run stubs `fetch` and records each request in the compared log.

**H4: `singleClickEdit` on `object-grid` is authored, not host-paired.** Unlike `DataTableSchema` (round 5), the spec's `object-grid` row declares it ("Enter cell edit on single click (default true when editable)"), and the grid supplies its own save path. So it is mirrored here, by reference to the row member, and round 5's runtime-only filing was not copied across.

**Authored census.** objectui: an AST and JSON walk over 497 JSON files, 1561 Markdown fences and 6083 TS/TSX files, with controls `object-grid` bag `objectName` 31 and `table.columns` 15. It found no document writing any of the eleven in an `object-view` `table` slot (two typed tests only). In an `object-grid` bag, three doc fences write keys this round mirrors: `operations` in `README.md` and `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`, `singleClickEdit` in `content/docs/plugins/plugin-grid.mdx`. The in-code producers are `ObjectView` (the relayed keys), `FieldDesigner` / `ObjectManager` (`operations`) and the plugin-grid demo. `resizableColumns` is written nowhere. objectstack `main` `3a6d92f7` (read by `git grep` on a self-named ref): its two authored `object-grid` nodes, the showcase work queues, write `objectName` / `columns` / `filter` only, and nothing in it authors an `object-view`.

## What changed

`packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`, the flat `ObjectGridSchema` mirror:

| key | member | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `grouping` | the spec's `GroupingConfigSchema`, by reference | kept unexamined | judged; a padded field name is refused by the spec's own rule |
| `navigation` | the spec's `NavigationConfigSchema`, by reference | kept | judged (the `table` slot still refuses it by name) |
| `rowColor` | the spec's `RowColorConfigSchema`, by reference | kept | judged |
| `rowHeight` | the spec's `RowHeightSchema`, by reference | kept | the five presets only |
| `reorderableColumns`, `singleClickEdit` | the row's own boolean members, by reference | kept | boolean |
| `aggregations` | strict `{ field, type }` entry, restating the twin | kept | judged; unknown member named |
| `operations` | strict six-toggle object, restating the twin | kept | judged; a misspelt toggle named |
| `bulkActionDefs` | strict entry restating `BulkActionDef`; `operation` and `visible`'s second arm by reference to the spec | kept | judged |
| `conditionalFormatting` | the two-dialect rule, now one private declaration shared with `ListViewSchema`'s mirror | kept | judged |

- The ten members are those the TypeScript twin declares, so `NarrowerThanDeclared` and `WiderThanDeclaredKeys` measure nothing new, and no `KnownDrift` or `WiderThanDeclared` row was added. The spec row types seven of the ten as `unknown`. Binding those would have mirrored nothing, so each member takes the spec schema the twin names, or the twin's own shape.
- `bulkActionDefs` is NOT the spec's `BulkActionDefSchema` by reference. Measured against the twin, that schema is narrower on `params` (a strict entry with a closed `type`) and on `visible` (no `ExpressionWire` arm), so binding it would have needed a `KnownDrift` row.
- `ListViewSchema`'s `conditionalFormatting` now reads the hoisted rule. Its accept set is unchanged, and the zod `ListViewSchema` member is the same union.

`packages/types/src/objectql.ts`: only `singleClickEdit`'s comment. It said `@default false`, but `ObjectGrid` reads `schema.singleClickEdit ?? true` and the spec row says the default is true.

`packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`: the `ObjectGridSchema` entry goes from eleven keys to `resizableColumns`, with the round's route written on it. The four pinned figure sites and the history sentences moved with it (header bullet 5 / 6; both ledger docstrings 6 keys; totals line 5 / 6 with 3 / 4 and 2 / 2; the spec-derived bullet 3 / 4).

**Doors, before and after:**

| door | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| authored `object-grid` (`properties` bag) | the spec row judges | unchanged |
| `object-grid` prop written flat on the node | refused by name | unchanged |
| `object-view` `table`, strict face (`objectui validate`) | the nine refused as unknown keys | a declared value parses; a wrong one is refused at the key |
| `object-view` `table`, tolerant face (`safeValidateSchema`) | any value kept unexamined | a wrong value refused at the key |
| `ObjectGridSchema.safeParse` directly | kept | judged |

## Pins

- New `packages/types/src/__tests__/unmirrored-declared-round6-6152.test.ts` (49 rows). For each key it checks that the mirror accepts the declared value and refuses a wrong one at the key, then drives the nine slot keys through the `table` slot on both faces. It holds that `table.navigation` / `table.resizableColumns` stay refused by name, and that the authored node does not move (flat refused by name, bag parses). It pins the two row members by identity, the spec's padded-name rule reaching `grouping`, the shared conditional-formatting rule by identity with `ListViewSchema`'s, and the strict entries naming unknown members. It also holds that `resizableColumns` is not a member.
- `grouping-field-padded-refused-7347.test.ts`: the census now finds `table.grouping` on `object-view`, as the 2026-09-30 evidence comment on #6152 predicted for the first round that mirrored this key. The table slot gets its own row and so carries the padded-field refusal on every face (the row type gained an optional `type` so one arm can own two paths).
- `imported-defaults-8317.test.ts`: the four new spec crossings are registered, and the mirror reads the row's members through the boundary (`stripImportedDefaults(SpecObjectGridPropsSchema).shape.KEY`).

## Corpus and pending changesets re-judged

- The three doc fences above write their keys in the `object-grid` bag, which the spec judges and this round does not touch. `content/docs/plugins/plugin-view.mdx`'s `table` section lists the relayed keys as declared, and the validator now agrees with it. No corpus document needed a change.
- `.changeset/11276-object-grid-properties-bag.md` (pending) said the row declares eleven keys "the flat mirror does not". This round makes that false for ten, so it gets a dated, append-only correction note (+2 / -0, frontmatter and every prior line byte-identical, checked by `cmp`). `check:changeset-claims` named 41 more pending changesets. Their paragraphs about the grid, the table slot and the ledgers were re-read, and none is made false.

## Reverse verification (predictions written first; objectstack `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, wrap mode, on committed `437408ce`; each restore proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`)

- **A1**, the `grouping` member deleted from the mirror (anchor x1 to x0, blob `36a2f818` to `dd46877a`): `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exit 2 with exactly one TS2322, `"objectql.zod.ts#ObjectGridSchema"` not assignable to `never` at the ledger reconciliation. vitest 22 failed, exactly as predicted: 4 in the round-6 pin, and 18 in the 7347 file (the census plus the table row on four faces).
- **A2**, `grouping` put back in the ledger entry with the mirror intact (blob `a93e249d` to `d0959519`): `tsc` exit 2 at the same reconciliation. The parity file had 2 runtime failures, the objectui#7279 split/totals pin and the objectui#8243 docstring pin. The prediction named #7279 and "possibly" #8222; the second one to fire was #8243.

No dist leg: every subject here resolves to source (relative imports in the types tests, and the root vitest alias for consumers).

## Tests and gates (final head `437408ce`; heavy runs through `os-verify-lock.sh`; each exit code captured before any pipe)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit`, `-p tsconfig.examples.json`, `-p tsconfig.test.json`, which judges the ledgers): exit 0.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/`: `Test Files 336 passed (336)`, `Tests 8904 passed (8904)`.
- Zod-face consumers outside `packages/types`: every test file that imports `@object-ui/types/zod` or names `safeValidateSchema` / `AnyComponentSchema` / `StrictAnyComponentSchema`. That is 115 files (schema-catalog, cli, app-shell previews, apps/console, components, scripts and twelve plugin packages), run in two halves: `58 passed (58)` / `1286 passed`, then `57 passed (57)` / `1015 passed`.
- The doc-snippet build closure (`turbo run build --concurrency=2`, the filter `check-doc-snippet-types.mjs --build-filter` prints): `Tasks: 35 successful, 35 total`. Then `check:doc-snippets` ("776 of 776 block(s) judged, 0 failed"), `check:doc-examples`, and `check:readme-exports`: all exit 0.
- All exit 0: `check-changeset-presence` ("6 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)"), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite` (report-only; the one appended note), `check:changeset-claims` (report-only), `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` ("0 new citation(s)"), `check:spec-symbols`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:element-data-source-declaration`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check-type-check-coverage` ("43/43"), `check:doc-types`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:component-surface-parity` (report-only), `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the diff (NOT GOVERNED).
- Lint, a declared narrowing: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 6 changed TS files. The JSON judged 6 files with no ignore notice: 0 errors, and 38 warnings, every one on a pre-existing line (0 on an added line). `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions` / `projectService`, and no `eslint-rules/` file reads the disk, so the diff cannot move an untouched file's verdict. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- `main` was merged once before this PR (`54be4dda`, bringing in objectui#11485, #11486 and #11482); the parity file merged with no conflict.

NOT MEASURED: `check:sdui-registration-pins` (it needs a console build, and no registration input moved); the full `pnpm test` farm and the repo-wide lint (CI's); `plugin-grid` / `plugin-view` behaviour suites (no runtime file changed). The contract record is the seat's to owe on the landing head.

## Open question: `resizableColumns`

The seat's answer A on #6152 ("`resizable` is canonical; the local half tombstones `resizableColumns`; its spec half forks to objectstack") was given while the flat mirror was the authored `object-grid` arm. Since objectui#11276 the authored node's props live in the spec's `properties` bag, which is `ComponentPropsMap['object-grid']` by reference and still declares `resizableColumns` ("Alternate spelling of `resizable`"). Pinned by objectui#11276: "the bag is the spec row by reference". So the local half as written would tombstone the TypeScript member and the mirror, and drop `ObjectGrid`'s `?? schema.resizableColumns` read. That leaves `objectui validate` and `os validate` both accepting `properties.resizableColumns`, with the flat refusal pointing at it, and nothing reading it. Measured: no document in either repository writes the key. The options, with four axes, are in the report on the card; this PR leaves the key in the ledger.

## Acceptance notes (noted, not filed here)

- The spec's `object-grid` row types seven of these keys as `unknown`, so the authored bag accepts `properties: { rowHeight: 'comfortable' }` or `grouping: 42` on both faces. `ObjectGrid` then falls back silently (for `rowHeight`, to `compact`). objectui#11276's PR already reported the row's `unknown` members as a spec-row finding. The report on the card names it for the seat with its measured reach.
- `BulkActionDef` / `BulkActionParam` (the TypeScript twin) are wider than the spec's `BulkActionDefSchema`: open params with any `type`, `ExpressionWire` predicates, and the runtime `actionDef`. The mirror follows the twin. A narrowing of the twin would be its own question.
- The strict face closes undeclared keys at every depth, including a `bulkActionDefs` param's catch-all that the twin and the tolerant face keep. That is the strict face's own construction, not this member's.
